newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Gazprom asks offshore firm to halt deals.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Gazprom asks offshore firm to halt deals.

text.p: Russian gas monopoly RAO Gazprom on Tuesday asked Cayman Islands-based Regent GAZ Investment Co to suspend an issue of Regent shares backed by Gazprom script until Gazprom lawyers decide whether or not this is legal under Russian law.

"We have recommended to the heads of the firm that they halt these transactions until our legal consultants study the documents they have received and take their decision," said Eduard Ivanov, head of the Gazprom's securities section.

Gazprom received a memorandum on Monday from Regent saying Regent subsidiaries would buy Gazprom shares worth $200 million on the Russian market in a bid to make Regent's own shares attractive to investors looking to profit from the rise in Gazprom shares on the Russian domestic market.
Ivanov said that, although it was too early to say what legal steps could be taken against Regent, there could be problems under the Russian law that regulates the circulation of Gazprom shares.

"Gazprom management considers that such transactions contradict Gazprom policies on dividing Gazprom shares between the domestic and foreign markets and are incompatible with Gazprom's strategy of issuing its shares in the form of American Deposit Receipts (ADRs)."
Gazprom is one of Russia's most illiquid shares and traders on the domestic market must receive permission from the company for almost every transaction.
Gazprom launched its American Depositary Receipt (ADR) programme on October 22, 1996, raising $430 million.
Gazprom closed at $0.47 on the Russian Trading System on Tuesday.
Domestic shares trade below the price of ADRs. Each ADR is backed by 10 shares.
